what: released PDE-Transformer sc-s fine-tuned with the paper's recipe (upstream main.py, separate channels, one-step supervised MSE, EMA 0.999) on the task's turbulent-radiative-layer training pool; best-validation checkpoint exported by environment/reference/pde_transformer_finetune/export_package.py and replayed through tests/main_verifier.py
protocol: task protocol: canonical split (environment/data/split.json), all 1,185 held-out cases, sealed contract; the model conditions on one frame (upstream sc-s recipe, timesteps=2), so it is given the last of the four context frames; per-dataset model, only the well/turbulent_radiative_layer_2D group is a real forecast

training.stopped_by: dataloader workers terminated under host memory pressure at epoch 43; the best-validation checkpoint (epoch 42) is the one packaged
training.initialization: released sc-s checkpoint (thuerey-group/pde-transformer @ d5889aab), i.e. an external-target reference, not a from-scratch row
deviations_from_the_recipe: none: the recipe runs as written for this dataset

normalization.what: the fine-tune's data pipeline normalizes with MeanStdNorm (normalize_data: mean-std, normalize_const: mean-std), so the package applies the same statistics, taken from the converted training file, and inverts them on the output
normalization.correction: an earlier replay of this checkpoint fed raw physical values and scored VRMSE 6.7539 on this group; that number was a harness error, not a property of the fine-tune

interpretation: 1.1680 on its own dataset beats persistence (1.3600) but remains well behind the from-scratch CNextU-net (0.6743). The sc-s recipe conditions on a single frame (timesteps=2) and is trained on a one-step objective, so a 30-step free-running rollout compounds error quickly, while The Well's recipe consumes four frames. This is the same protocol effect the DPOT rows show: a model built for a different context length is handicapped here, and the row is reported as such rather than as a ceiling.

metadata_class_correction.what: upstream encodes the Fields and Constants entries of physical_metadata as indices into two fixed vocabularies (pdetransformer/data/metadata_remapping.py), not positionally. A first export numbered them 1..N, which loads the right weights and runs without error while conditioning the model on embeddings the fine-tune never saw.
metadata_class_correction.note: the number reported above is the corrected one; export_package.py now calls upstream's converters

derivation.what: recomputed on 2026-09-22 from this report's own per-dataset means after removing the corpus family 'ape2d/hyp' (upstream ships hyp.hdf5 as a content copy of diff.hdf5); per-dataset numbers are the measured ones, group means and the reward follow score.py's aggregation exactly; case counts are the canonical split's (environment/data/split.json); the per-dataset means come from the run's verifier report.json and are now embedded
